The specified commands (--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare) will source the PKGBUILD and download the AppImage, but will not execute prepare(), build(), or package(). No malicious behavior occurs during this gate. The provided sha256 checksum is a real hash (not SKIP), so the download will be verified against it.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for upstream.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR package maintainer helper script for the kdenlive-appimage package. It performs three routine functions: detecting the latest upstream version by scraping KDE's download directory, downloading the AppImage to calculate its SHA256 checksum, and updating the PKGBUILD with new version information. All network requests target `download.kde.org`, which is KDE's official download server and the expected upstream source. Temporary files are properly created with `mktemp -d` and cleaned up with `rm -rf`. The script only downloads and hashes the binary—it never executes any downloaded content. No obfuscation, data exfiltration, or unexpected system modifications are present. This is a typical automation script for package maintenance workflow.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR update helper script for kdenlive, fetching from KDE upstream.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard packaging practices for an AppImage-based package. The source is downloaded from the official KDE download site (download.kde.org), and the sha256 checksum is properly pinned to a specific hash (not SKIP). The prepare() function extracts the AppImage using its built-in --appimage-extract feature, which unpacks the AppImage locally without any network download. The package() function installs the AppImage binary, a simple wrapper script, icons, and a desktop file into $pkgdir using standard install commands. No dangerous operations are present: no curl/wget downloads during build, no eval or base64-encoded blobs, no obfuscated commands, no modification of system files outside pkgdir, and no network requests during the build or package phases.

The wrapper script in /usr/bin/ is a straightforward exec of the AppImage binary with pass-through arguments, which is a common and expected pattern for AppImage packages. The icon and desktop file installation iterates over standard hicolor icon sizes from the extracted squashfs-root, which is normal behavior. This file is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging for an AppImage-based application and shows no evidence of injected malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AppImage PKGBUILD from official KDE source, no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
